newsitem.title: UK: UK CBI sees no need for major labour law reform.
newsitem.headline: UK CBI sees no need for major labour law reform.

text.p: The Confederation of British Industry (CBI) said the current framework of industrial relations law in Britain was a sound basis for good employee relations and it did not need further major reform.
Responding to a government green paper on industrial action, CBI director of human resources John Cridland said:
"The CBI believes that there is a need to minimise disputes in key industries...but this is more likely to be achieved through the further extension of competition rather than more legislation."

The government's latest plans, which go further than the radical curbs introduced when Margaret Thatcher was prime minister, would allow trade unions to be sued if a strike causes "disproportionate or excessive effects."
Cridland said the government's proposals would lead to more uncertainty in the workplace.
"CBI members do not believe that all the proposals should be taken forward, although the ideas on re-ballotting union members during long disputes are worthy of further consideration," he added.
